title: SLO Adoption Catalyst: Roadmap & Team Playbook (Q4 2026 initiative draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures a lightweight, tactical roadmap plus a playbook to accelerate SLO adoption across product and infra teams. Focus = make SLOs practical (measurable, actionable, and minimally overhead) for 10 priority services during Q4 2026 and establish repeatable rituals for org-wide scale in 2027.

Audience:
- Primary: Eng leads, SREs, Product managers owning candidate services.
- Secondary: Console, Observability, Solutions Eng, Customer Success (for downstream SLAs).

High-level goals (success criteria):
- 10 services onboarded with baseline SLOs, dashboards, and error-budget policies by end of Q4 2026.
- 80% of those teams using the SLO playbook templates for incident response and rollouts.
- Reduce P99 latency regression incidents across onboarded services by 30% (quarter over quarter).
- SLO maturity metric: average maturity score >= 3/5 across onboarded teams.

Principles (do not over-engineer):
- Start with one critical SLO per service (availability or latency depending on user-facing behavior).
- Keep SLO formulas transparent and reproducible (shared PromQL/metrics queries).
- Make error budgets operational (automated alerts + human runbook actions).
- Iterate quickly: small wins, instrument, improve.

Key components of the playbook (what each team must deliver)
1) SLO spec template (required)
   - Owner, service description, user-facing dimension, measurement window, SLI definition (PromQL where applicable), target (e.g., 99.9% over 30d), error budget burn policy.
   - Example: "API v2 request success rate (4xx+5xx) excluding maintenance windows": PromQL snippet included.
2) Dashboard and SLI export
   - Minimal SLO dashboard with current SLI, error budget remaining, burn rate chart, 30/7/1 day views.
3) Alerting and automation
   - Two alert thresholds: advisory (50% burn rate) to product + SRE, and critical (100% burn) to oncall + exec.
   - Playbook step for automated throttling or fallback if applicable.
4) Runbook actions mapped to error budget state
   - For advisory: schedule joint triage + review change queue.
   - For critical: invoke temporary capacity/burst policy and pause non-essential feature rollouts.
5) Oncall responsibilities and escalation matrix
   - Who owns initial triage, who owns mitigation, who decides feature pauses.

Adoption roadmap (waves)
- Wave 0 (Nov 2025 – Jan 2026): Pilot with 3 services (auth, serving-runtime-core, embeddings-index). Confirm templates, PromQL guards, and dashboard plumbing.
- Wave 1 (Feb 2026 – Apr 2026): 4 more services (console api, upload service, dedicated-provisioning, routing). Focus on SLI parity and alert tuning.
- Wave 2 (May 2026 – Jul 2026): Expand to 6 additional teams; introduce error-budget automation hooks.
- Acceleration wave / Q4 push (Aug 2026 – Dec 2026): Finish remaining priority services, run cross-team drills, and lock SLO ownership into team charters.

Tactics to drive adoption (practical initiatives)
- SLO clinic: weekly 1-hour drop-in with SREs to help teams write PromQL, instrument SLIs, and create dashboards (book via internal scheduler).
- SWAT rotations: 1 SRE embedded per product team for 2 weeks during initial rollout for pairing and runbook creation.
- Office hours + recorded templates: short how-to videos (10–15m) and copy-paste dashboard JSONs.
- Incentives: feature-gating policy: new features must include SLI impact note before rollout.
- "SLO champions" program: nominate one engineer per team and give a small budget for training + recognition.

Operational mechanics (who does what)
- SRE core (eng-site-reliability): run SLO clinic, maintain templates, provide dashboards and alert playbooks.
- Observability team: support metric ingestion, dashboard hosting, templated panels.
- Product owners: decide user-facing dimensions and sign off SLO targets.
- Platform/Infra: provide capacity/burst knobs, define emergency scaling playbook.

Maturity ladder (1–5) — lightweight scoring that teams will self-report
1 = no SLI instrumentation.
2 = SLI instrumentation + simple dashboard.
3 = SLO configured + alerts + runbook.
4 = Error budget ops automated + disaster mitigation playbook tested.
5 = SLO tied into release gating + continuous improvement loop and evicence of quant improvement.

Example runbook snippets (copyable)
- Triage step 1: check SLO dashboard (30d window). Confirm metric source and any known maintenance windows.
- Triage step 2: check recent deploys (GitHub PR list) and high-change services.
- Mitigation step: if error budget burn > 100% and cause = traffic surge: enable backpressure or route to read-only replicas (link to runbook PR).
- Post-incident: fill SLO incident template and schedule a 2-week follow-up to confirm corrective action.

Instrumentation notes (PromQL examples)
- Availability SLI (synth): sum(successful_checks) / sum(total_checks) over 30d.
- Latency SLI (p99): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,job)) but aim to use pre-aggregated percentile metrics where possible.

Alerts (recommended thresholds)
- Advisory: error_budget_burn_rate > 0.5 for 6h => page to product-slo channel and SRE oncall (P4).
- Critical: error_budget_remaining < 0 over 1h => page oncall + exec email + create SEV ticket (P1).

Communication plan
- Announcement: product + infra town hall (30m) at wave start.
- Weekly status email with adoption scoreboard to eng leads.
- Bi-weekly cross-functional sync: 30m brown-bag to share learnings.
- Slack channel: #slo-adoption (SREs + champions) for quick Q&A.

Training and learning
- 2-hour hands-on workshop per wave: write an SLO, create dashboard, configure alerts (record session).
- Short self-serve playlist: PromQL basics, SLO design tradeoffs, error budget ops checklist.

Automation and tooling ideas (backlog)
- CLI tool to generate SLO spec from service manifest.
- Auto-generate PRs that add SLI dashboards when a service opts in.
- Robot to enforce feature gating via release pipeline if SLO is in critical burn.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: teams treat SLOs as compliance checkbox. Mitigation: scorecard + leaderboards + tie into roadmap planning conversations.
- Risk: noisy alerts lead to alert fatigue. Mitigation: staged alerts + tuning window + SRE-assisted onboarding.
- Risk: metric fidelity issues. Mitigation: observability audits during clinic and mandatory metric ownership in spec.

Next steps (short-term, immediate owners)
- Finalize SLO spec template (owner: Ben Huang) — due 2026-03-20.
- Schedule pilot SWAT embeds for 3 pilot services (owner: Aisha Patel) — start 2026-03-28.
- Create SLO clinic calendar and signup page (owner: Rosa Meyer) — live 2026-03-17.
- Prepare initial dashboards and PromQL examples and publish repo of JSON panels (owner: Liam O'Connor) — due 2026-03-31.

Notes to self / loose ideas (work-in-progress)
- Consider linking SLO maturity to Quarterly Eng OKRs to drive adoption beyond SRE inertia.
- Look into adding small telemetry tag to rollout tickets to mark SLO-aware deploys.
- Ask legal/finance about whether we should map certain SLOs to contractual SLA tiers for enterprise customers.

Open questions (for leadership sync)
- Should SRE own enforcement of feature pausing or should product leads hold that authority?
- What threshold of adoption triggers shifting to "enterprise enforcement" (automated gating)?

Appendices (links and quick references)
- Pilot service list (internal): auth, serving-runtime-core, embeddings-index.
- Quick checklist: SLO spec + dashboard URL + alert policy + runbook link + champion name.

Draft status: This is a pragmatic working doc intended to be iterated with product and platform partners. Please add feedback inline or in #slo-adoption.
